title: Embracing the future of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom: the relevance of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking in modern education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper discusses the role of artificial intelligence in education, with a focus on AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking. It asks how educators and institutions can respond to the rapid adoption of large language models such as ChatGPT and how students can be guided to use them responsibly in academic work and classroom learning.

The paper combines a conceptual discussion with informal observations from the author’s experience at a Swiss University of Applied Sciences (Kalaidos University of Applied Sciences) and a narrative literature review. It describes an institutional response in the form of AI guidelines for student writing, emphasizing transparency about model use, prohibition of direct copy-pasting, and the need for critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs. It also proposes workshops, updated guidance, and dedicated staff support as ways to build an AI culture at the institution.

A second major focus is pedagogical: the paper lays out what AI literacy should include, such as understanding AI basics, limitations, bias, ethics, and practical use, and it presents prompt engineering methods as instructional tools for improving learning and critical thinking. The paper concludes that simply allowing or banning AI is insufficient; instead, schools should teach students and teachers how to use AI critically and responsibly. It also suggests that AI literacy should be accessible to all learners, though this is presented as a recommendation rather than an evaluated intervention.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based generative AI chatbot for conversational text generation and assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Discussed as a major AI chatbot used in education and as an example of an LLM students and teachers might use for academic work, prompt engineering, and classroom activities. The paper also mentions GPT-4 and other OpenAI models under this umbrella.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual discussion and narrative literature review, not an empirical K-12 study with comparison groups or measured outcomes. It contains no subgroup analyses or outcome data for literacy effects.
impact_tier_rationale: No quantitative effects are reported, so there is no measurable impact on literacy or subgroup outcomes to assess.
